svg.text: taia.ds — a connected component: the browser and the REPL, one in-chan
a click (POST) and a server event (send-event!) enter the same flow, and run the same controller and view

g.text: You write two things: a controller and a view
The controller is a state machine of plain functions; the view is a render fn, ctx → hiccup.
taia.ds does the rest: the routes, the flow and its chans, the SSE stream, send-event!, the morph.
A connected component: one in-chan, two ways in
The live counter page opened an SSE stream, so its flow stays up.
The browser and the server both send it events through the same in-chan.
{"live1": {"count": 1, "state": "displayed"}}; increment takes the count from the memory: 1 → 2.
The view renders the new ctx, and the POST is answered with it: the tab shows 2,
The REPL: the same event, into the same in-chan
(ds/send-event! "live1" "demo-user" "increment" {:count 2}): a server event has no request
and no signals, so the REPL sends the memory as params. It answers true at once.
increment takes the count from the params this time: 2 → 3. Nothing is kept on the server.
Down the open stream, into the page
Nobody asked this time, so the render is pushed down the page's SSE stream. The tab shows 3,
and its signals hold {"live1": {"count": 3, …}} for the next click.
A click and a send-event! are the same kind of message, handled by the same controller and view.
You wrote those two; the route, the flow, its chans and the stream are taia.ds.
